subject: SLO fitment calc and HW tradeoffs — next steps and validation plan
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLO fitment calc and HW tradeoffs — next steps and validation plan

Hi Alan,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good alignment on the app surface and performance goals. Quick written recap so we have an agreed starting point and a minimal validation plan we can run together.

Recap of HelioBank goals (as discussed):
- P95 latency target: <= 150ms for streaming responses (live chat flows, progressive tokens)
- Sustained throughput: ~120 requests/sec (peak bursts to ~200 rps)
- Concurrency per model: ~12 concurrent in-flight sessions (KV cache warms expected)
- Quality: using a 7B conversational model variant; preferring open models with quantization where possible

Initial Redwood sizing hypothesis (for Dedicated reservation):
- H100 (1x) cluster: best headroom for sustained rps and tight p95s for longer sequences
- A100 (80GB) (1-2x): good throughput cost tradeoff for batch-friendly workloads; slightly higher p95 at small batch sizes
- L4 / T4-class (multi-tenant / smaller instances): cost-effective for scale but likely to miss 150ms p95 on streaming flows at your concurrency

What we propose as next steps (validation plan):
1) Baseline synthetic runs — we’ll run 30m steady-state tests on each candidate hw (H100, A100, L4) using your typical prompts and token lengths. We’ll capture p50/p90/p95/p99 and token cost.
2) Replay test — use a 1-hour replay of a sampled real traffic trace (you can provide anonymized traces or we’ll sample during a 1-hour production window).
3) Streaming sanity run — 2-hour test with progressive token streaming to validate client-side observed time-to-first-byte and p95 streaming latency.
4) Acceptance criteria: p95 <= 150ms for streaming in the production-like replay AND sustained 95% of target throughput for 60% of the run.

I’m attaching a short fitment matrix (slo-fitment-matrix-20270521.xlsx) describing the expected tradeoffs and a short validation playbook we’ll run on Redwood Dedicated.

Can you confirm:
- Are those p95 and throughput numbers the right targets for procurement?
- Do you have an anonymized traffic sample we can use for the replay? If not, we can schedule a 1-hour capture window.

If that looks good I’ll loop Ben (SE) for a quick sizing sketch and Marissa for billing/commit framing. We’ll aim to get a 2-hour validation slot on Redwood Dedicated next week.

Thanks,
Karthik

Thanks Karthik — this captures our goals well. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we lock the validation window:

- The 150ms p95 target is for the user-facing streaming experience (time-to-first-token + streaming tail). Internally we tolerate up to ~250ms for server-side completion if needed.
- For throughput: 120 rps sustained is our normal traffic; we need the system to withstand 2x for promo spikes.
- On traces: we can provide a sanitized 2-hour trace (production sample) by EOD tomorrow. Will that be sufficient?

Also procurement will want: an estimate of reserved throughput (tokens/min or rps-equivalent) and a cost delta between the H100 and A100 options so we can model ops spend.

If Ben or Marissa can sketch the committed throughput units and a short runbook for the validation steps that will help our procurement/infra teams.

Best,
Alan

Subject: Re: SLO fitment calc and HW tradeoffs — next steps and validation plan

Alan — quick technical sketch and an initial committed throughput suggestion. Formatting inline for quick review.

Short answers to procurement asks:
- Suggested reserved throughput (starting point): 8,000 tokens/sec (~480k tokens/min) which maps to ~140 rps for average response lengths we discussed (3.4k tokens/session equivalent across streaming). We can scale reserved units up after validation.
- Cost delta (monthly committed): H100 cluster (~$XXk/mo higher than A100 for same slot count). I’ll share a pro forma cost sheet in the next email (Marissa will add exact pricing tiers).

Hardware tradeoffs (practical summary):
- H100: best single-stream latency and headroom for bursty traffic. On our internal tests H100 maintained p95 streaming =~ 120–140ms at 150 concurrent sessions on a 4-node pool. Good for your 2x burst buffer needs.
- A100 (80GB): strong throughput per dollar for batched workloads. p95 tends to be ~160–220ms in streaming at 12 concurrent sessions unless you tune batching aggressively. Better cost if you can accept slightly higher p95 tail under burst.
- L4-class: cost-optimized; expect to miss 150ms p95 consistently for streaming use-cases with your concurrency, not recommended for primary. Good for background embedding/low-priority inference.

Validation runbook (what our team will run with you):
1) Prep (Day 0): exchange sanitized traffic sample and model artifacts (quantized checkpoint if using a q4 route).
2) Synthetic microbench (1h each hw): measure token throughput, p50/p90/p95/p99 streaming, kernel overheads.
3) Replay (2h): run your 2-hr sample on each hw variant under the Dedicated reservation and capture full traces + client-observed TTFB.
4) Failure mode checks (30m): inject 2x burst and soft-fail to model fallback to a cheaper variant; verify graceful degradation.
5) Post-run analysis: we’ll produce an acceptance report with cost per 1M tokens and recommended commit.

Attachments: attached a short PDF with the Redwood Dedicated validation playbook and the fitment matrix Karthik referenced.

Action items for HelioBank:
- Send anonymized trace (Sanjay) — target EOD tomorrow.
- Confirm your procurement contact (procurement@heliobank.com copied above?) so Marissa can share pricing worksheets and preliminary commit math.
- Suggest 3 available 2-hour windows next week for the validation runs; we’ll block one and provision the cluster.

Ben Carter
